svg.title: Acute leukemia: recognition and urgent decision points
svg.desc: An original educational flowchart. Suspected acute leukemia requires smear, marrow, flow cytometry and genetics. Suspected APL takes an urgent ATRA and coagulation-support path. Other cases require lineage and risk assessment; ALL also needs a dedicated CNS plan. Differentiation syndrome requires prompt steroids and severity assessment.

g.text: ACUTE LEUKEMIA • URGENT DECISIONS
Original IntMed teaching algorithm • teacher review pending
Cytopenia, bleeding, fever or blasts
Do not rely on the WBC count alone
Smear + marrow + flow cytometry + genetics
In parallel - never delay ATRA if APL is suspected
Assess bleeding, infection, leukostasis and organ function
APL suspected?
Abnormal promyelocytes + coagulopathy
Send PML::RARA / t(15;17)
Other acute leukemia
Establish AML vs ALL lineage
Genetics and response guide the next plan
Urgent ATRA + coagulation support
Do not delay for every final report
Regimen selection is risk / protocol based
Risk-adapted systemic treatment
ALL: a dedicated CNS plan is also needed
A TKI alone does not replace CNS prophylaxis
During ATRA / arsenic: watch for differentiation syndrome
Fever + weight gain / edema + dyspnea / hypoxemia → prompt steroid + assess severity
Severe cases may need a temporary drug hold and organ support • no routine leukapheresis in APL
Educational summary, not a stand-alone treatment prescription • source page references are retained in the topic
